title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a recto page of handwritten notes for the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' (c. 1965). The neighbouring pages are the typescript on the reverse, an English translation of a paper on line bundles and ample divisors, and are unrelated. The page treats real and archimedean structure in a motivic Galois formalism. The setting appears to be the following, reconstructed from the notation on this page only. G is the global motivic Galois group, with identity component G°. For each 'point' s' (apparently a place, here an archimedean one) there is a local group G(s'). There is a twisted form G^{ξ(s')} of G, obtained by a twist ξ(s') (a torsor, or a fibre functor at s'). There is also a homomorphism u(s'): G(s') -> G^{ξ(s')}, the local datum, a Frobenius- or Hodge-type morphism.

(1) G°_R carries a 'polarisation' π. In modern terms this is a Cartan involution, i.e. a compact real form up to conjugacy. Grothendieck notes it is equivalent to a homomorphism i: μ_{2,C} -> G°_C, the Weil-operator, an element of order 2 up to centre.

(2) At s', G(s')_C carries a cocharacter i(s'): G_{m,C} -> G(s')_C, the Hodge or weight cocharacter. Restricting to μ_2 ⊂ G_m and composing with u(s') gives v(s') = u(s')_C ∘ (i(s')|μ_2): μ_{2,C} -> G^{ξ(s')}_C.

(3) The required compatibility: the polarisation π^{ξ(s')} of G^{ξ(s')}_R, obtained by transporting π along the twist ξ(s'), must equal the polarisation defined by v(s'). Grothendieck stresses that this is a non-tautological condition, and that it constrains u(s').

(4) A bracketed caveat follows. One must check how the classes of polarisations of a group H are described by homomorphisms μ_{2,C} -> H_C, which are defined only up to conjugation, and the group is not commutative in general. The margin reads '? à vérifier', and there is a sub-case 'si G est commutatif'.

(5) Finally, by the 'conjectures de Tate magnifiées', knowing the u(s') should recover the effectivity structure in the category of motives. That is, which motives are effective should be detectable from local Frobenius and Hodge data.

The problem served is to axiomatize the motivic Galois group together with its local, place-by-place realizations, including the archimedean place and polarizations. The aim is a description of the category of motives over a global field by a group-plus-local-data package, from which even effectivity could be read off.
errors: Gap: the Weil operator C = h(i) satisfies C^2 = h(-1) = weight parity ε, which is central but not necessarily trivial. So a polarisation corresponds to an order-2 homomorphism only into the adjoint group, or to μ_4 -> G with a fixed central ε. 'μ_2 -> G_C' is exact only modulo the centre. Grothendieck himself flags uncertainty ('? à vérifier', 'non commutatif en tous cas').

The correspondence between conjugacy classes of homomorphisms μ_2 -> H_C and polarisations of H_R is not a bijection in general. The homomorphism must also be compatible with the real structure, i.e. defined over R up to inner twisting. The page does not resolve this.

Calling this 'i|μ_2' of the cocharacter needs care: the Weil operator is h(i), the image of i ∈ S(R) = C^*. It is not the image of -1 under a cocharacter, which would give only ε. The page's formulation is heuristic.

ideas.what: Polarisation of a real reductive (motivic Galois) group, identified with an element/homomorphism μ_2 -> G_C (Cartan involution via Weil operator)
ideas.modern_name: Polarization of a Tannakian category over R; Cartan involution ad C; Deligne's criterion for polarizable Hodge structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne-Milne (1982), Deligne (Hodge II, Travaux de Shimura)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own published texts; written up by Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, LNM 265) from Grothendieck's program

ideas.what: Compatibility condition: the global polarisation transported by the twist ξ(s') must equal the one induced by restricting the local Hodge cocharacter (through u(s')) — non-tautological constraint on local morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Axiom 'ad h(i) is a Cartan involution' (Shimura datum axiom SV2); archimedean condition in Langlands-Rapoport's admissible morphisms of Galois gerbes

ideas.what: Global motivic group with local morphisms u(s'): G(s') -> G^{ξ(s')} at each place, twisted by local fibre functors/torsors
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois gerbe with local Weil/Frobenius/Hodge morphisms (Langlands-Rapoport pseudomotivic gerbe; Taniyama group with local data)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's motivic Galois ideas are known mainly through Saavedra and Récoltes et Semailles mentions

ideas.what: 'Magnified Tate conjectures': local data u(s') determine the effectivity structure (which motives are effective)
ideas.modern_name: Effectivity detected by realizations (integrality of Frobenius eigenvalues / Hodge numbers ≥0); consequence of Tate + generalized Hodge conjectures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; discussed by Grothendieck (generalized Hodge conjecture), later Kahn, Ayoub and others

missed.claim: Around 1965 Grothendieck formulates a global motivic Galois group with local morphisms u(s') into twisted forms G^{ξ(s')}. At the archimedean place he imposes that the polarisation induced by the restricted Hodge cocharacter equal the transported global polarisation. This is structurally the archimedean admissibility condition of Langlands-Rapoport's Galois-gerbe formalism (1987), and Deligne's axiom that ad h(i) be a Cartan involution. The anticipation is not documented as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: il faut que π^{ξ(s')} (polarisation de G^{ξ(s')}_R déduite de π ...) soit celle définie par ... v(s') ... une condition non tautologique ... sur u(s')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically it shows the 'local morphisms + polarization compatibility' architecture of Langlands-Rapoport / Milne's motivic gerbes existed in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes. It also bears on the treatment of non-commutative groups, an issue he flags explicitly.

missed.claim: He asserts that, under strengthened Tate conjectures, the family of local data u(s') recovers the effectivity structure on motives. The thread is stated without development.
missed.quote: Enfin, conformément aux conjectures de Tate magnifiées, la connaissance des u(s') permet de retrouver la structure d'effectivité dans la catégorie ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Detecting effectivity from realizations (an 'effectivity conjecture') is still discussed. An explicit early formulation in terms of local Galois/Hodge data could interest people working on motivic t-structures and effectivity.

deep.surprise_reason: The polarisation and Tannakian ideas are known to descend from Grothendieck via Saavedra. The explicit place-by-place compatibility of polarisations with local morphisms u(s'), and the claim that local data recover effectivity, are notable unpublished details anticipating Deligne's and Langlands-Rapoport's formalisms. But they are sketchy and partly unverified by Grothendieck himself.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'De plus, on a une structure polarisée π sur G°_R' — the superscript π at top right is the name of the polarisation.
'qui en fait équivaut à définir via un homomorphisme i: μ_{2,C} -> G°_C' (the crossed-out word is 'définir').
Second map: i(s'): G_{m,C} -> G(s')_C (domain is G_m, not μ_2).
'par suite par conjugaison' is possibly 'par suite, par composition' (unclear in image); it introduces v(s').
In the bracket: probably 'en termes d'un homomorphisme μ_{2,C} -> H_C, qui est ... défini à conjugaison près ... non commutatif en tous cas!'
